title: The Third Quarter: Deep Sleep
meter: Prose (the Upanishad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Mandukya Upanishad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pada and matra, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
devanagari: यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते
translation: Where the sleeper desires nothing and sees no dream, that is deep sleep. The third quarter is Prajna: its field is deep sleep, where everything has become one; it is a mass of awareness, made of bliss, enjoying bliss, with consciousness as its mouth.
translation_hi: जहाँ सोया हुआ व्यक्ति न कोई इच्छा करता है और न कोई स्वप्न देखता है, वह सुषुप्ति है। तीसरा पाद प्राज्ञ है: उसका क्षेत्र सुषुप्ति है, जहाँ सब एक हो जाता है; वह प्रज्ञा का घन है, आनंदमय है, आनंद का भोक्ता है और चेतना ही उसका मुख है।

words.note: ghana = dense; in maths, ghana = cube (घनमूल = cube root)!

grammar: Ghana = dense and cube: the Upanishad's 'dense mass of awareness' uses the same word Bhaskara uses for a cube, because a cube is 'solid'.
-maya 'made of': आनन्दमय, like the five koshas: annamaya, pranamaya, manomaya, vijnanamaya, anandamaya (Nirvana Shatkam verse 2).
Science link: deep, dreamless sleep shows as slow delta waves on an EEG, about 0.5 to 4 Hz: the brain's slowest rhythm.
